answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly and reputation transferable: each agent stakes value before it can act, so creating a new fake identity means burning real resources. Track each agent's behavior as a delta from network norms — small honest deviations keep earning trust, while a sudden spike flags a bot farm. Like an island linked by a trellis of peer attestations, no single node vouches alone; endorsements must accumulate across independent neighbors, making bulk fake identities economically useless.
